title: Structure à l'infini des Mg,ν [pages 1 à 90, dont table des matières] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (cote 147, the 'structure at infinity' of M_{g,ν}). X = D_0 is a complex-analytic space, in the intended application the Deligne–Mumford compactification of M_{g,ν} as an orbifold or stack, with its boundary stratification. For each d, D_d is the normalised ('déployé') closure of the codimension-d stratum. If the stratification comes from a normal crossings divisor D, then D_d is the space of pairs (x, unordered set of d local branches of D through x). D_{d,d'} (d ≥ d') is the finite étale cover of D_d obtained by also choosing d' of these d branches; it maps to D_d and to D_{d'}. The previous pages attach to each D_d a normal 'tangent' object T_d, a torus group G_d and a torsor P_d. The torsor is essentially the bundle of normal tori, i.e. the punctured normal bundle (C^*)^d or its circle version (S^1)^d. These are pulled back along the flag spaces D_{d,d',d''}, which gives tautological transitivities.

On this page he introduces the first non-tautological structure, which uses the normal-crossings hypothesis.
(i) Suppose the stratification comes from a normal crossings divisor D on X = D_0. Then for every d the induced stratification on D_d again comes from a normal crossings divisor Θ_d on D_d. Θ_d is the trace of the branches other than the d chosen ones. Its strata are the D^{<d>}_i := D_{d+i,d}, and its complement is D_d^*, the open stratum of points lying on exactly d branches.
(ii) Likewise D^*_{d,d'}, the preimage of D_d^* in D_{d,d'}, is the complement of a normal crossings divisor Δ(d,d') on D_{d,d'}.
(iii) With P_d^* = P_d restricted to D_d^*, one can then define a canonical 'homomorphism of generization' r_{d,d'}: π_1 P_d^* → π_1 P_{d'}^* for d' < d.

Modern reading: P_d^* is a model of the 'link' of the open stratum D_d^*, namely a deleted tubular neighbourhood of D_d^* intersected with X∖D. It is homotopy equivalent to an (S^1)^d-bundle over D_d^*. Its π_1 is an extension of π_1(D_d^*) by Z^d, or by Ẑ(1)^d in the étale setting.

How the map arises. Near D_d^*, after choosing d' of the d branches (a point of D^*_{d,d'}), moving off the remaining d−d' branches lands in D_{d'}^*. The (S^1)^d-bundle over D^*_{d,d'} splits as (S^1)^{d'} × (S^1)^{d−d'}. The second factor is the deleted normal neighbourhood of D_d inside D_{d'}, which maps to D_{d'}^*. This gives a map of spaces from the pullback of P_d^* to D^*_{d,d'} into P_{d'}^*, hence the homomorphism on π_1, defined up to base point or inner automorphism.

Why it matters for the project. These maps are the 'specialisation/generisation' gluing data between the fundamental groups at infinity. The next page organises them into a semi-simplicial (1/2-simplicial) analytic space 𝒟_* built from the flag spaces D_{d_0 ≥ ... ≥ d_r}. That is the combinatorial skeleton for describing π_1 of M_{g,ν} 'at infinity', i.e. the boundary data feeding the Teichmüller-tower programme of the Esquisse.
errors: As literally written, r_{d,d'}: π_1 P_d^* → π_1 P_{d'}^* is not well defined. The natural map is defined on π_1 of the pullback of P_d^* to the finite étale cover D^*_{d,d'}, a finite-index subgroup. Equivalently it is a correspondence through D^*_{d,d'} (choice of d' of the d branches), not a map from π_1 P_d^* itself.

No base points are specified. The homomorphism exists only up to conjugation (an 'outer' map), unless tangential base points or groupoids are used. Grothendieck presumably intends fundamental groupoids, as elsewhere in these notes.
Minor: the equation number (203) is used and crossed out twice on this page, and reused for a different formula on the next page. The numbering is in flux.

ideas.what: Normalised strata D_d of a normal crossings divisor (d-fold self-intersections with choice of branches) and flag covers D_{d,d'}. The induced stratification on each D_d again comes from a normal crossings divisor Θ_d, with open part D_d^*.
ideas.modern_name: Normalisation of strata of an snc/nc divisor; the log stratification is preserved on strata
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard (Deligne, Hodge II, 1971, for D^{[d]}; folklore)
ideas.where_published: Similar notation appears in Deligne's Hodge II. Grothendieck–Murre (LNM 208) treat normal crossings divisors in the étale setting.

ideas.what: Torsor P_d^* over D_d^* (normal torus bundle restricted to the open stratum) as a model of the link of the stratum; its π_1 is an extension of π_1(D_d^*) by Z^d.
ideas.modern_name: Link / deleted tubular neighbourhood of a stratum; fibres of the Kato–Nakayama space X^log over D_d^*; real oriented blow-up
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical topology (Mumford, Hirzebruch); Kato–Nakayama 1999 for the log version; Grothendieck–Murre 1971 for tame étale π_1
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck–Murre LNM 208 (étale analogue). Esquisse d'un programme mentions tubular neighbourhoods at infinity of M_{g,ν}.

ideas.what: Canonical 'homomorphism of generization' r_{d,d'}: π_1 P_d^* → π_1 P_{d'}^* for d' < d, from the link of a deeper stratum to the link of a shallower one.
ideas.modern_name: Specialisation/generisation maps between fundamental groups of links; exit-path functoriality; tangential-base-point maps between boundary inertia groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Exit paths: MacPherson, Treumann, Lurie. Boundary inertia and tangential base points for M_{g,n}: Deligne, Ihara, Nakamura, Oda
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §§ on the Teichmüller tower and 'structure à l'infini', only informally

missed.claim: The system of torus torsors P_d^* over the open strata D_d^*, glued by generization maps and organised (next page) into a semi-simplicial space of flag strata, is in substance the Kato–Nakayama / real-blow-up description of X∖D near the boundary. It is also an exit-path-type π_1-system for the stratified space. Here it is written down specifically for M̄_{g,ν}, around 1981–84, as a tool to reconstruct π_1 at infinity.
missed.quote: On peut définir un homomorphisme canonique de généralisation π_1 P^*_d → π_1 P^*_{d'} pour d' < d
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It shows Grothendieck's 'structure at infinity' programme was built on what is now stratified/log homotopy theory. This is relevant to anabelian reconstructions of the Teichmüller tower from boundary data (Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki 'combinatorial anabelian geometry'). The specific simplicial packaging may still be worth comparing with those works.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is correct in substance and fairly standard: strata of normal crossings divisors, links as torus bundles, specialisation maps between their π_1. It is a documented ingredient of the 'structure à l'infini' programme. The mild interest is seeing the explicit generization maps and their semi-simplicial organisation anticipating Kato–Nakayama and exit-path ideas, but nothing a specialist would find unexpected.
transcription_corrections: 'la stratification analogique' is probably 'la stratification analytique'.
'en diplongeant celui-ci' is unclear. It is plausibly 'en déployant celui-ci' (Grothendieck's term for passing to normalised strata), and likewise 'stratification des déployements'.
'pour ne disposer des doublages en long et en large' is more likely '... je me dispense de développer en long et en large'.
The insertion over D_d reads 'Θ_d (sur D_d)': the normal crossings divisor on D_d is named Θ_d.
The bottom caption reads 'homomorphisme de généralisation', underlined.
